argument_summary: The defensible position from the current admissible record is not clean certification. It is limited certification with an explicit caveat. The evidence supports that overall launch readiness clears threshold by 2.3 percentage points and the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, but it also shows a remaining below-target environmental permit screening weakness concentrated in stormwater exception explanation, plus only a draft mitigation runbook with TBD owner and alert threshold. Under that record, the strongest supportable packet is: certify on a caveated basis only if the packet itself documents the limitation and describes the draft monitoring and rollback steps as risk-management support rather than proof of resolution.
claims_about_business_cost: A caveated certification posture avoids treating this record as a policy breach requiring further escalation when the remaining issue can be bounded through explicit disclosure and documented monitoring. That preserves launch progress more proportionately than treating the current draft mitigation as full closure or, conversely, escalating as though aggregate readiness evidence had no weight.
claims_about_policy: Enterprise policy controls here. It does not support certification without material caveats because there is neither evidence that no material weakness remains nor an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The same policy does permit a narrower position: if a material limitation remains, it must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance support disclosure and monitoring practices, but they do not replace the enterprise requirement. So the admissible policy-consistent reading is caveated compliance, not clean compliance.
concessions: The current record does not show approved risk acceptance.
The current record does not show a finalized mitigation with owner and alert threshold, so the draft runbook is not sufficient for caveat-free certification.
The model-card draft statement that there are no known material limitations is in tension with the unresolved slice issue and should not be defended as accurate on this record.
No new evidence is being added, and the current record does not prove that the required disclosure has already been completed.
